job.title: Senior Backend Engineer
job.jd_text: Northwind Analytics is hiring a Senior Backend Engineer to build the APIs and data pipelines behind our retail analytics platform. You will design and operate Python services built with FastAPI, store data in PostgreSQL, use Redis for caching, and run event-driven pipelines on Kafka. Services run in Docker on AWS. Requirements: 5+ years of backend development; strong Python; solid SQL and data-modelling skills; experience designing REST APIs; experience debugging production incidents; clear communication with product and data teams. Nice to have: experience with Kafka consumer groups and exactly-once processing.

questions.text: Walk me through how you would design a REST API for uploading and querying sales reports for thousands of retail stores.
A PostgreSQL query that used to take 50 ms now takes 5 seconds in production. How do you investigate?
How would you decide what to cache in Redis for a read-heavy analytics endpoint, and how do you keep the cache correct?
Tell me about a production incident you were involved in. What happened and what did you change afterwards?
How would you make a Kafka consumer process each event exactly once into PostgreSQL?
Describe a time you disagreed with a product manager about scope. How did you resolve it?
How do you structure a large FastAPI codebase so several teams can work on it?
What is your approach to writing tests for code that calls external APIs?

criteria.name: System design
criteria.description: Designs scalable, maintainable backend systems and explains trade-offs.

anchors.2: Basic design, misses major concerns such as scale or failure.

anchors.3: Methodical approach using the obvious tools.

criteria.name: Data and SQL

anchors.3: Solid fundamentals, can reason about indexes and plans.
anchors.4: Strong; reasons about locking, consistency, and data modelling trade-offs.
anchors.5: Deep expertise across modelling, performance, and correctness.

criteria.name: Communication
criteria.description: Explains ideas clearly and collaborates with non-engineers.

anchors.4: Clear, concise, adapts to the audience.
anchors.5: Exceptionally clear; structures complex ideas simply.

questions.text: Walk me through how you would design a REST API for uploading and querying sales reports for thousands of retail stores.
expected_signals: Defines clear RESTful endpoints, resource structures, and standard HTTP methods
Addresses high-volume ingestion using asynchronous processing or payload compression
Includes pagination, filtering, and rate-limiting strategies for query endpoints
Discusses data validation, error handling, and API security mechanisms
follow_up_probes: How would you handle rate limiting or throttling when thousands of stores submit simultaneously?
What trade-offs would you consider between synchronous validation and asynchronous background processing?

questions.text: A PostgreSQL query that used to take 50 ms now takes 5 seconds in production. How do you investigate?
expected_signals: Uses EXPLAIN ANALYZE to inspect execution plans and scan types
Investigates index usage, bloat, missing statistics, or stale autovacuum runs
Checks database metrics such as lock contention, CPU load, and memory usage
Considers dataset volume growth and data distribution changes
follow_up_probes: What specific PostgreSQL system views or parameters would you inspect first?
If EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows an unexpected sequential scan, what steps would you take to fix it?

questions.text: How would you decide what to cache in Redis for a read-heavy analytics endpoint, and how do you keep the cache correct?
expected_signals: Identifies optimal cache candidates using query frequency and latency metrics
Evaluates cache invalidation strategies like write-through, TTL-based expiration, or event-driven invalidation
Considers edge cases like cache stampedes, thundering herd, and hot key management
Explains cache eviction policies and memory allocation considerations
follow_up_probes: How would you prevent a cache stampede when a heavily accessed aggregate key expires?
How would you ensure consistency between Redis and PostgreSQL when analytics data updates?
